{{Top|leg|italics=1}}
{{Quote|No Mandalorian soldier should have to fight an ''aruetii''{{'s}} war for the price of a day's food. No ''Mando'ad'' should have to fight at all, except to defend ''Manda'yaim'', his home, or his family, or because he wants to. We have to stop being the tool of governments that don't care if we live or die so long as we do their bidding.|[[Venku Skirata]]|<ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>}}
'''''Kadikla''''' was a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] nationalist ideological movement that arose in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], and the aftermath of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]'s [[Battle of Mandalore (Yuuzhan Vong War)|assault]] on the Mandalorian's cultural [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. Headed by the Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Venku Skirata]]—often known under the nickname and alias of ''Kad'ika''—''kadikla'' was described by those familiar with the concept as a "Mandalore-first" movement. ''Kadikla'' advocated the need for Mandalorians to band together and put the greater good of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Mandalore and its people over the desires of the individual, establishing [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian space]] as a strong, independent state in which every Mandalorian could flourish. Several Mandalorians supported the ''kadikla'' movement, including [[Goran Beviin]], [[Graad]], members of [[Clan Skirata]], and numerous others. [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] was swayed into a tepid support following a meeting of the Mandalorian clans at [[MandalMotors Hall]] in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], during and after which he issued several edicts that aligned with ''kadikla'' ideals in pursuit of bettering Mandalore.

==Overview==
{{Quote|You got a better idea? Oh, wait—is this going to be the all-day diatribe on ''kadikla'' self-determination and statehood?|[[Baltan Carid]]|<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>}}
''Kadikla'' was an ideological movement that advocated a more nationalist stance for the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]] clans. While the clans had a history of banding together in times of need, the Mandalorians had largely been against the organized government and bureaucracy present in states such as the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]], due to their independent and often nomadic culture.<ref name="Bloodlines">''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]''</ref> Known colloquially as a "[[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]-first" movement, proponents of ''kadikla'' preached that while their nomadic traditions had served the Mandalorians well in the past, a strong, central, Mandalorian nation would be to the benefit of all,<ref name="Sacrifice" /> providing the nomadic Mandalorians a powerful citadel upon which they could rely and fall back upon,<ref name="Bloodlines" /> and one the aggressive factions of the [[galactic community]] would be remiss to attack.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

The goal of ''kadikla'' was to provide the members of the warrior clans—often employed by foreign powers as [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]]—with greater opportunities for success and self-determination.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Instead of hiring out their services to outside agencies that cared little for the lives of the soldiers in their employ, often out of a desperate need for [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] to provide for oneself and family, ''kadikla'' promoted the idea that a Mandalorian should never be forced to fight in order to make ends meet, establishing domestic opportunities for income. According to ''kadikla'', a Mandalorian soldier need only ever fight to protect oneself, their family, and [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]; mercenary work was still considered an acceptable means of acquiring income, so long as it was the choice and preference of the individual, rather than a necessity of last resort.<ref name="Revelation" />

==History==
{{Quote|We need to make sure we're warriors with a citadel to defend, so we can pick our battles and not rely on the whims of ''aruetiise''. Foreigners. It's the spirit of the times, like I said.''"<br />"''And who's driving this ''spirit of the times?"<br />"''Nobody, really. But there's this guy called Kad'ika that we're all hearing about. Thinks it's time we looked after ourselves—really looked after ourselves. Not just gather in the clans and unite when we're threatened, but build Mandalore itself into something new.|[[Goran Beviin]] and [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]|<ref name="Bloodlines" />}}
Named for the movement's founder, Kad'ika—the life-long nickname and alias of the soldier [[Venku Skirata]]—''kadikla'' found its roots<ref name="Sacrifice" /> in the ideas passed along to Skirata from his paternal [[Parent/Legends|grandfather]], [[Kal Skirata]].<ref name="ImpCom501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref> A veteran mercenary who had worked in the employ of a number of criminals and corporations,<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> the elder Skirata developed strong views on Mandalorian self-sufficiency<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> that he passed on to his grandson.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] by the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extra-galactic]] [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Species/Legends|species]], the [[Extragalactic/Legends|alien]] invaders launched an [[Battle of Mandalore (Yuuzhan Vong War)|assault]] on the Mandalorian's cultural homeworld of Mandalore in [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Though the Mandalorians were able to repel the Yuuzhan Vong attack successfully, the planet and its people had suffered significantly, to the point that Mandalore continued to bear the scars of the battle more than a [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] later. It was in the aftermath of this devastation that ''kadikla'' began to take root.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Influenced by his grandfather's philosophy,<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> Venku Skirata began speaking before groups of Mandalorians, spreading the ideals of ''kadikla'' across Mandalore and making a name for himself, as the movement gained notable traction in a community ravaged by the Yuuzhan Vong.<ref name="Bloodlines" /> Skirata was supported by the members of [[Clan Skirata|his clan]],<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and came to sway a large number of other Mandalorians,<ref name="Bloodlines" /> winning over the likes of the [[Mandalorian Supercommando|Mandalorian supercommando]] [[Goran Beviin]], and other influential members of the culture such as [[Neth Bralor]] and [[Graad]]. Graad, himself, became a vocal supporter of ''kadikla'', known amongst his peers for breaking into lengthy discussions on the movement's merits.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], a meeting was held at [[MandalMotors Hall]] in Mandalore's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]], [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]], wherein a multitude of clan [[Chief/Legends|chieftains]], local [[Chief Executive Officer/Legends|business owners]], and other prominent Mandalorians met with [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], the reigning [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']]—traditional leader of the Mandalorian clans. Discussing the state of Mandalore and Mandalorian affairs, ''kadikla'' principles were offered both by Neth Bralor and Graad, though the movement was derided by [[Baltan Carid]] and a number of their fellows at the meeting. Despite the dissenting opinions of Carid and a few others, Fett took an interest in the ideals of ''kadikla'' that Graad put forward, and subsequently made several decrees in line with the movement, including recalling two million Mandalorians from around the galaxy to replenish Mandalore's diminished population. Venku Skirata praised Fett's decision when the two soldiers met some [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] later,<ref name="Sacrifice" /> though Skirata continued to speak before gatherings of clan leaders on the ideals of ''kadikla'' in the hope that the movement might gain greater acceptance.<ref name="Revelation" />

==Behind the scenes==
''Kadikla'' was first introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] via an indirect mention in the second entry in the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' novel series. Entitled ''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]'', the novel was [[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Karen Traviss]] and published [[August 29]], [[2006]]. The movement was later named in Traviss' subsequent entry in the ''Legacy of the Force'' series, ''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]'', published a year later on [[May 29]], [[2007]], before appearing again in the penultimate novel in the series, ''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]'' published [[February 26]], [[2008]].
